transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling customer service. How can I help you today?
Customer: Hi there. I was checking my card activity and noticed something weird from a gas station recently.
Agent: I would be happy to take a look at that for you. May I have your name, please?
Customer: Yes, my name is Ivan Delacroix.
Agent: Thank you, Mr. Delacroix. For verification, could you confirm the last four digits of the card you're inquiring about?
Customer: It's 4109.
Agent: Thank you. Can you tell me what you're seeing on your account that seems off?
Customer: Well, back on September 29th, I stopped to get gas at QuickFuel 214, and there are two charges showing up for $61.20.
Agent: You see two separate charges for $61.20 from QuickFuel 214 on September 29th?
Customer: Yes, exactly that. But I only got gas once.
Agent: Did you have any trouble at the pump, like having to swipe or insert your card a second time?
Customer: No, nothing like that. I put my card in, filled up my tank, grabbed the receipt, and left. 
Agent: Did you purchase anything inside the convenience store, or was it strictly fuel at the pump?
Customer: Strictly fuel. I never went inside. 
Agent: And does the receipt you kept show $61.20?
Customer: Yes, it shows one purchase for $61.20.
Agent: Have you contacted QuickFuel 214 about the duplicate transaction appearing on the account?
Customer: No, I haven't reached out to them yet. I just saw it on my online account and decided to call you guys first.
Agent: All right. So to make sure I have all the details noted properly, on September 29th you bought gas at QuickFuel 214 for $61.20, but you see that identical amount posted twice on your card.
Customer: Yes, that's exactly what happened.
